methodological_rigor.justification: Cross-sectional single-center survey of 100 women with HR+ early breast cancer on adjuvant endocrine therapy, using the validated SMAQ. Eligibility criteria are clearly defined and consecutive recruitment minimizes selection bias within the attending population. Authors explicitly note that the sample size was pragmatic (no a priori calculation), acknowledge that the SMAQ has not been formally validated in adjuvant breast cancer, and perform a parsimonious multivariable logistic regression with VIF-based collinearity checks. Comparisons between endocrine agents are not adjusted for line of therapy, and treatment sequence bias is acknowledged. Self-report with single time point limits causal inference and captures behavior, not persistence.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Single-center cross-sectional survey maps to Oxford LoE 4. Clinically relevant for regional Australian oncology services where adherence data are limited, and findings (side-effect burden, forgetfulness) have practical implications for intervention design (reminder systems, breast care nurse support, proactive side-effect management). However, findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational cross-sectional study; STROBE applies. Reporting includes clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, outcome assessment (SMAQ), statistical methods, univariable and multivariable analyses, VIF reporting, and an explicit limitations section. Ethics approval text is REDACTED (partially due to blinding) rather than omitted by authors. STROBE checklist not explicitly referenced. Supplementary Table S1 (VIF) is referenced. No data-availability statement for survey data and no details of IRB number or funding in the normalized text.

novelty_literature.justification: Adherence to adjuvant endocrine therapy in breast cancer is an extensively studied topic with multiple SMAQ-based studies (refs 26-29) and systematic reviews (ref 17). The novelty is the regional Australian setting, which fills a documented geographic evidence gap in the authors' health system. Findings largely replicate prior barriers (forgetfulness, side-effect burden) with no novel methodology or mechanism.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well written, organized with clear IMRaD structure, and plainly presents context, methods, results, and limitations. Tables and a figure are referenced logically. Discussion sections are appropriately subtitled and each subsection builds on the previous. Statistical results include effect sizes, p-values, and 95% CIs where appropriate. Minor issue: 'Univariate analyse using t-test' typo, and age IQR '(IQR: 51.8-62.9)' appears inconsistent with median 62.5 (upper bound equals median). Otherwise polished.

key_strengths: Addresses a documented gap: adherence patterns in regional Australian breast cancer care
Uses the validated SMAQ and reports both univariate and multivariable analyses with collinearity diagnostics
Transparent acknowledgement of limitations, including SMAQ validation gap, self-report bias, and treatment sequence confounding for between-drug comparisons
Appropriately cautious interpretation of the exemestane finding after multivariable adjustment
Clear clinical implications: reminder systems, nurse-led support, proactive side-effect management
key_concerns: Small single-center cohort (n=100) with no a priori sample size calculation limits statistical power and generalizability
Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference and persistence assessment
Key confounders (socioeconomic status, distance to services, comorbidities, side-effect severity) not captured
SMAQ not formally validated for adjuvant endocrine therapy; self-report likely overestimates adherence
Novelty is geographic rather than methodological; findings replicate established barriers
Age IQR inconsistent with the stated median 62.5 (upper bound 62.9) suggesting a reporting error
chief_reviewer.rationale: A transparently reported but modestly novel cross-sectional adherence study in regional Australia; fits Tier 3 (e.g., BMC Cancer, Asia-Pacific J Clin Oncol) with minor revisions to correct typographical issues and clarify sample-characteristic numbers.
